mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£3,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £2,500-£4,500 depending on the engine code (M9R 760 vs M9R 820) and labour rates. Used engines: £600-£1,500. Reconditioned: £1,300-£2,800. Rebuilt with warranty: £1,800-£3,500. Fitting labour: 8-12 hours at £65-£100/hr.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of turbo actuator failure on a Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are loss of power and increased fuel consumption. The wastegate actuator arm can seize, preventing the turbo from generating boost. Loss of power when accelerating. Increased fuel consumption. Engine management light. Turbo not boosting - actuator arm stuck.

mainEntity.name: Does the Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 dCi (M9R engine) uses a timing chain, not a belt. This is a significant reliability improvement over the 1.9 dCi which uses a belt. The chain should be inspected from approximately 200,000 km (124,000 miles). Timing chain - not a belt. Inspect from 200,000 km. Chain can stretch over time.

mainEntity.name: Is the Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 dCi (M9R) is generally more reliable than the 1.9 dCi, with the timing chain being a significant improvement. However, it has known issues with the EGR valve, DPF and turbo actuator. With regular maintenance, the engine can last 150,000+ miles. More reliable than 1.9 dCi. Timing chain is a major improvement. EGR/DPF issues are common. Regular maintenance is essential.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 2.0 dCi engine codes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Laguna 2.0 dCi was offered with several M9R engine codes: M9R 760 (173 hp, Laguna II, 2005-2007), M9R 700 (150 hp, Laguna III), M9R 815 (175 hp, automatic, 2008-2015) and M9R 820 (180 hp, GT line, 2008-2015). M9R 760: 173 hp, Laguna II. M9R 700: 150 hp, Laguna III. M9R 815: 175 hp, Laguna III auto. M9R 820: 180 hp, Laguna III GT.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and what has failed. For a 2005-2015 Laguna 2.0 dCi worth £1,500-£6,000, a £1,800-£3,500 rebuilt engine is usually worthwhile if the car is otherwise sound. Turbo actuator or EGR failure often makes repair more cost-effective than full replacement. Cars worth £2,500+: rebuilt engine with warranty is recommended. Cars worth £1,500-£2,500: evaluate both options carefully. Turbo actuator failure: repair is usually cheaper than replacement. Cars worth under £1,500: consider used engine or scrap.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 2.0 dCi was introduced to the Renault Laguna II range in 2005 as a more powerful diesel alternative to the 1.9 dCi, using the Nissan-developed M9R engine family. It continued into the Laguna III (2007-2015) with various power outputs from 150 hp to 180 hp, becoming the flagship diesel engine for the range. The M9R engine uses a timing chain rather than a belt - a significant reliability improvement over earlier Renault diesel engines.

milestones.description: M9R 760, 2.0-litre turbo diesel, 173 hp (127 kW) - Laguna II 2.0 dCi launch engine
M9R 700, 2.0-litre turbo diesel, 150 hp - Laguna III launch diesel engine
M9R 815, 2.0-litre turbo diesel, 175 hp - Laguna III automatic variant
M9R 820, 2.0-litre turbo diesel, 180 hp (131 kW), 400 Nm torque - GT line flagship diesel

commonProblems.h2: Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi (M9R engine family) is generally more reliable than the 1.9 dCi, with a timing chain rather than a belt. However, it has specific, well-documented issues - particularly around the EGR system, turbo actuator and DPF. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbo Actuator Failure - The Most Common Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi Problem
problems.rootCause: The wastegate actuator arm can seize, preventing the turbo from generating boost. The arm for the wastegate actuator doesn't move when started or when revving, and the arm can become stuck solid. Loss of power and increased fuel consumption are common symptoms. The boost pressure regulator solenoid valve may also malfunction.

repairOptions.longevity: If actuator is seized but turbo is intact
If turbo has suffered consequential damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2005-2015 Laguna 2.0 dCi is worth £1,500-£6,000 depending on mileage and condition. For a sub-£2,500 example, a £350-£650 actuator replacement is a sensible repair. If the turbo has failed, a rebuilt engine with warranty (£1,800-£3,500) may be the most cost-effective option.
problems.recommendation: Turbo actuator failure is a known issue on M9R engines. If you're experiencing loss of power or increased fuel consumption, have the turbo system inspected immediately. Actuator replacement at £350-£650 specialist cost is significantly cheaper than a full turbo replacement. Check all vacuum pipes for leaks first - these are often the cause of actuator problems.
problems.cta: -> Compare Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi turbocharger replacement costs

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Clogging - Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi (all M9R variants, particularly Euro 5 models)
problems.rootCause: Soot buildup is the biggest problem causing the EGR valve system to fail. Soot ends up in the flap through which the valve regulates the amount of exhaust gas that goes back into the engine. A stuck EGR valve can result in a total loss of power. DPF regeneration failure is also common on urban-driven vehicles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve and intake

repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix if valve is faulty

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Forced DPF regeneration or chemical clean

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Laguna 2.0 dCi worth £1,500-£6,000, a £200-£650 EGR or DPF repair is a justifiable expense if the car is otherwise sound.
problems.recommendation: EGR and DPF issues are extremely common on Laguna 2.0 dCi models. Regular motorway driving helps keep the DPF clear. If you're experiencing poor low-speed response, black smoke or limp-home mode on highway runs, have the EGR valve inspected. A simple clean may resolve the issue - specialist cost £200-£400.
problems.cta: -> Compare Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi EGR and DPF replacement costs

problems.h4: Timing Chain Inspection - Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Laguna 2.0 dCi (all M9R variants) Typical inspection mileage: 124,000 miles (200,000 km)
problems.rootCause: The M9R engine uses a timing chain rather than a belt - a significant reliability improvement. However, the chain can become overstretched and require replacement. Based on real-life experience, the timing chain change interval is approximately 200,000 km. It is recommended to check the condition of the chain periodically after this mileage and replace it if it becomes excessively stretched or if unusual engine noises occur.

repairOptions.longevity: If chain is stretched or rattling

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: If chain has failed causing valve/piston damage
repairOptions.longevity: Catastrophic failure; often the only option

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For most Laguna 2.0 dCi examples, a £700-£1,200 timing chain replacement is a significant but justifiable investment if the car is otherwise sound.
problems.recommendation: The M9R timing chain is generally more reliable than a belt, but it does need periodic inspection. If you hear unusual engine noises or have covered over 200,000 km, have the chain inspected. Preventative replacement at specialist cost is far cheaper than a full engine replacement.
